extracted.intended_audience: researchers in computer science / machine learning / artificial intelligence looking for reviewer opportunities or wishing to contribute call-for-reviewer links
extracted.subtask_description: A GitHub README that aggregates current 'call for reviewers' links for top CS/ML/AI conferences and journals, and explains how to contribute new calls to the list. Useful for researchers seeking review experience or ways to advertise reviewer calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This project aims to collect the latest 'call for reviewers' links from various top CS/ML/AI conferences/journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the repository to find reviewer calls across conferences and journals in CS/ML/AI. The README lists 'Current Calls for Reviewers' with dates and links; maintain scope to relevant top CS/ML/AI venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended reviewer profile / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are doing research in the computer/machine learning/artificial intelligence fields and want to accumulate reviewing experience (e.g., to apply for NIW/H1B/EB1 or to improve your CV), consult and use this repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository targets active researchers in CS/ML/AI who seek reviewer experience. (Chinese text reiterates same target audience.)

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contribute to the repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Fork this repository, add new 'call for reviewers' links to the README.md file, ensure link format is clear and includes relevant information, then submit a Pull Request. Alternatively, email jiahaoli57@163.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-by-step contribution procedure: 1) Fork the repo; 2) Add call links to README.md; 3) Keep link format clear and include relevant info; 4) Submit a PR or email the maintainer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link formatting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure the link format is clear and includes relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should provide links with enough context (conference/journal name, role being recruited, date/deadline, and any tag such as CCF/CORE category) so readers can quickly assess relevance. (Page requests clear format but gives no strict template.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits to participating reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating as a reviewer is a way to engage with the academic community, apply for NIW/H1B/EB1, enhance your CV, and stay updated with the latest research trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The README notes additional perks for some conferences: outstanding reviewers may have the opportunity to waive next-year registration fees. Other entries mention occasional honoraria (e.g., NASA: reviewers eligible for $350/day). Use these benefits as part of decision to volunteer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / maintain current calls
rubrics_metrics.description: The README organizes 'Current Calls for Reviewers' by date (e.g., 2026.02.06, 2026.01.19, etc.), implying the list should be kept up-to-date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding calls, include the date and update the 'Current Calls' section so readers can find active/ongoing calls quickly. The presence of many dated entries signals that timeliness is a quality requirement for contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term / evergreen reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A section titled 'Long-term validity 长期有效' lists reviewer/editor programs that are continuously open or long-term (e.g., ACM TIST & IEEE TNNLS, Applied Intelligence, NASA, MDPI Reviewer, Elsevier Reviewer, Springer Reviewer, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perennial reviewer programs separately from time-limited conference calls so users can find ongoing opportunities; flag their 'long-term' status when adding them to the README.
